items.title: Freedom From Deceit, and Rarely Ill

items.zh: 云何名為無有諂曲？謂有純質，為性正直，於其大師及諸有智同梵行所，如實自顯。如是名為無有諂曲。云何名為少諸疾病？謂性無病、順時變熟、平等執受、不極溫熱、不極寒冷、無所損害，隨時安樂。由是因緣，所食、所飲、所噉、所甞、易正變熟。如是名為少諸疾病。
items.en: What is meant by freedom from deceit? It means being genuinely simple and upright by nature, showing oneself truthfully before the Teacher and before wise fellow practitioners of pure conduct. This is called freedom from deceit. What is meant by being rarely ill? It means being naturally healthy, digesting food properly in season, maintaining an even balance [of body and mind], neither too hot nor too cold, without harm, at ease at all times. Through this cause, what one eats, drinks, chews, and tastes is easily and properly digested. This is called being rarely ill.

items.zh: 云何名為性勤精進？謂能安住有勢、有勤、有勇、堅猛，於善法中能不捨軛，翹勤無惰，起發圓滿，能有所作，於諸有智同梵行者躬自承奉。如是名為性勤精進。云何名為成就妙慧？謂聰、念、覺、皆悉圓滿。根不闇鈍、根不頑愚、亦不瘖瘂，非手代言，有力能了善說、惡說所有法義，具足成就俱生覺慧，具足成就加行覺慧。如是名為成就妙慧。
items.en: What is meant by diligence by nature? It means abiding with strength, with sustained effort, with courage, with steadfastness, never abandoning the yoke of wholesome practice, ever diligent and never lazy, generating complete energy, seeing tasks through to completion, and personally attending upon wise fellow practitioners of pure conduct. This is called diligence by nature. What is meant by accomplished excellent wisdom? It means cleverness, mindfulness, and realisation, all complete: faculties neither dull nor obstinate, neither mute nor reliant on gesture in place of speech, capable of distinguishing well-spoken teaching from poorly-spoken teaching, fully accomplished in both innate wisdom and wisdom cultivated through effort. This is called accomplished excellent wisdom.

items.zh: 云何少欲？謂雖成就善少欲等所有功德，而不於此欲求他知。謂他知我具足少欲，成就功德。是名少欲。云何喜足？謂於隨一衣服、飲食、臥具等事，便生歡喜，生正知足。於所未得所有衣服，或麁或妙，更無悕望、更無思慮；於所已得不染不愛，如前廣說而受用之。如於衣服，於其飲食、臥具等事，當知亦爾。
items.en: What is having few desires? It means that, although one has accomplished the qualities of having few desires and the like, one has no wish for others to know of it — no wish that others should know "I have few desires, I have accomplished these qualities." This is called having few desires. What is contentment? It means that, regarding whatever robe, food, bedding, or the like one happens to receive, one feels genuine joy and correct contentment. Regarding robes not yet received, whether coarse or fine, one has no further hope or concern for them; regarding those already received, one uses them without attachment or craving, exactly as explained at length before. As with robes, so too with food, bedding, and the like.

items.title: Section: Easy to Support, Easy to Satisfy, and Ascetic Virtues Open

items.zh: 云何易養？謂能獨一自得怡養，不待於他，或諸僮僕、或餘人眾。又不追求餘長財寶，令他施者、施主等類謂為難養。是名易養。云何易滿？謂得微少，便自支持；若得麁弊，亦自支持。是名易滿。云何成就杜多功德？謂常期乞食、次第乞食、但一坐食、先止後食、但持三衣、但持毳衣、持糞掃衣、住阿練若、常居樹下、常居逈露、常住塚間、常期端坐、處如常坐。如是依止若食、若衣、若諸敷具杜多功德，或十二種，或十三種。
items.en: What is being easy to support? It means being able, on one's own, to sustain oneself contentedly, without depending on others, on servants, or on any retinue; and not seeking further wealth beyond what is needed, so that donors never find one difficult to support. This is called being easy to support. What is being easy to satisfy? It means that, receiving only a little, one is content to sustain oneself with it; and receiving something coarse or poor, one is likewise content to sustain oneself with it. This is called being easy to satisfy. What is accomplishing the virtues of ascetic practice? Regularly begging for alms, begging in sequence, eating only one sitting's worth, eating only before a fixed time, keeping only three robes, wearing only wool, wearing only discarded rags, dwelling in the forest, dwelling constantly beneath a tree, dwelling constantly in the open, dwelling constantly near a charnel ground, always sitting upright, and remaining in one's fixed seat. Depending on whether counted by food, robe, or bedding, the virtues of ascetic practice number either twelve or thirteen.

items.title: Begging for Food: Neither Favouring the Rich Nor Favouring the Poor

items.zh: 於乞食中分為二種。一者、隨得乞食，二者、次第乞食。隨得乞食者，謂隨往還家，隨獲隨得而便受食。次第乞食者，謂入里巷，巡家而乞，隨得隨現而便受食。不高舉手越趣餘家，願我當獲精妙飲食，乃至期願多有所得。
items.en: Begging for alms is of two kinds: begging as it comes, and begging in sequence. Begging as it comes means that, going to whatever households one customarily visits, one receives and eats whatever is obtained there. Begging in sequence means entering the lanes and alleys and going from house to house in order, receiving and eating whatever appears, not raising the hand [in refusal] and passing over one household for another in hope of obtaining finer food, still less hoping to obtain a great deal.

items.zh: 當知此中，若依乞食無差別性，唯有十二；若依乞食有差別性，便有十三。云何名為但一坐食？

items.title: Eating Once, Eating Before a Fixed Hour, and Owning Only Three Robes

items.zh: 謂坐一座，乃至應食悉皆受食，從此座起必不重食。如是名為但一坐食。云何名為先止後食？謂為食故，坐如應座，乃至未食先應具受諸所應食。應正了知：我今唯受爾所飲食，當自支持。又正了知：我過於此，定不當食。如是受已，然後方食。如是名為先止後食。云何名為但持三衣？謂但三衣而自支持。何者三衣？一、僧伽胝，二、嗢怛囉僧伽，三、安怛婆參。除此三衣，終不貯畜過此長衣。如是名為但持三衣。云何名為但持毳衣？
items.en: Eating only one sitting's worth means receiving and eating whatever food is appropriate while seated, and once risen from that seat, never eating again. Eating only before a fixed time means sitting properly to eat, first fully receiving all the food to be eaten, and clearly resolving: I shall take only this much food to sustain myself, and beyond this I will certainly not eat. Owning only three robes means sustaining oneself with three robes alone: the great robe, the middle robe, and the inner robe — and never keeping any further robe beyond these three.

items.title: Coarse Wool Only, and Robes Sewn From Discarded Rags

items.zh: 謂所持衣或三衣數、或是長衣，一切皆用毛毳而作，終不貯畜餘所作衣。如是名為但持毳衣。云何名為持糞掃衣？謂所有衣，他捨棄擲或街、或巷、或市、或鄽、或道非道，或雜便穢，或為便穢、膿血、洟唾之所塗染。取如是等不淨衣物，除去麁穢，堅執洗浣，縫染受持。
items.en: Wearing only wool means that whatever robes one keeps — whether the three basic robes or any further robe — are all made of coarse animal hair, never any finer material kept in store. Wearing only discarded rags means taking cloth others have thrown away in the street, the alley, the marketplace, a dwelling, on a road or off it, cloth soiled with filth, blood, pus, mucus, or spittle — taking such unclean cloth, removing the coarsest dirt, washing it with real care, and sewing and dyeing it into a robe to be kept and worn.

items.zh: 如是名為持糞掃衣。云何名為住阿練若？

blocks.text: More ornaments, then the **ascetic practices** (dhūta, 杜多), voluntary simplicities that "shake off" attachment.

**Freedom from deceit**: "genuinely simple and upright by nature, showing oneself truthfully before the Teacher". **Rarely ill**: "naturally healthy, digesting food properly in season, maintaining an even balance, neither too hot nor too cold". Venerable Miào Jìng reads the "even balance" also of the mind: meeting anything without greed or hatred.

"Abiding with strength, with sustained effort, with courage, never abandoning the yoke of wholesome practice." Wisdom: "cleverness, mindfulness, and realisation, all complete", able to tell well-spoken teaching from poorly-spoken, with both innate and cultivated wisdom.

"Although one has accomplished the qualities of few desires, one has no wish for others to know of it." Master Cháng Bǎi: real few-desires does not advertise itself. Contentment: satisfied with whatever robes, food, and lodging come.
"Able to sustain oneself contentedly, without depending on others", so that donors never find one difficult.

Twelve or thirteen, depending on how they are counted. Regarding food: **begging for alms** (as it comes, or house by house in order; Master Cháng Bǎi: some disciples favoured the rich, others the poor; the Buddha taught going in order); **eating at one sitting**; **not eating after a fixed time**. Regarding robes: **only three robes**, **only coarse wool**, **only rag robes**.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish 諂 and 曲 in "freedom from deceit"?
options: 諂 is outward amiability, 曲 is inner twisting
quiz.why: "Being genuinely simple and upright by nature, showing oneself truthfully before the Teacher and wise fellow practitioners." Venerable Miào Jìng: 諂 is the outward manner — seemingly amiable — while inside there is 曲, many hidden twists.

quiz.q: How do the masters explain "even maintenance" (平等執受) in being rarely ill?
options: Miào Jìng: greed and hatred unmoved in all situations; Cháng Bǎi: the body held by the storehouse consciousness stays in balance
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: meeting anything without greed or hatred — equal reception, greed, hatred, and delusion unmoved. Master Cháng Bǎi: the body held by the storehouse consciousness undergoes no imbalance and continues evenly.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call having few desires?
options: having such qualities without wishing others to know
quiz.why: "Although one has accomplished the qualities of having few desires and the like, one has no wish for others to know of it." Master Cháng Bǎi: not displaying one's virtue is having few desires; a practitioner with merit should not let others know, but stay humble.

quiz.q: How many ascetic virtues are there, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain twelve versus thirteen?
options: twelve or thirteen — merge four food practices into three and you get twelve; keep them apart, thirteen
quiz.why: "Depending on whether counted by food, robe, or bedding, the virtues of ascetic practice number either twelve or thirteen." Venerable Miào Jìng: in the food group, merge four into three and you get twelve; separate them, thirteen.

quiz.q: Sequential begging skips no house. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say the Buddha thought of favouring the poor or the rich?
options: the Buddha said neither is appropriate
quiz.why: "Begging in sequence means entering the lanes and alleys and going from house to house in order." Master Cháng Bǎi: some disciples favoured the poor over the rich, others the rich over the poor; the Buddha said neither was appropriate.

quiz.q: Eating one sitting means never eating again after rising. The note says not even if interrupted. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: if one leaves midway on urgent business, on returning one may perform the "leftover-food procedure" and continue
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if, halfway through, something urgent calls one away, on returning to continue eating one should perform the leftover-food procedure — the opposite of the note.
